stages.title: Conductor.Planning library + agnostic rules block + policy seam
stages.notes: Deliver P0 per docs/history/CONDUCTOR-PLANNER.md (P0). KEYSTONE - build the decoupled home FIRST so everything else lands in it. REUSE, do not fork: WorkflowEngine is already nearly pure; the workflow/override model + WorkflowRuntimeVars already exist; IPlanner shows the DI pattern. Net-new: (1) new project src/Conductor.Planning/Conductor.Planning.csproj that does NOT reference Conductor (engine); move the planning-domain model types + the pure WorkflowEngine into it; keep BuildRuntimeVars engine-side as a thin adapter that builds the POCO. (2) a declarative `pipeline` PipelineRules block on PlanConfig with defaults that reproduce today EXACTLY (absent block = byte-identical run). (3) IWorkflowResolver seam with a default impl in Conductor.Planning, wired via ConductorHost DI; engine calls the interface. (4) DELETE the dead AgentConfig.TokenCeiling (audit: defined+merged but enforced nowhere; the ai-native plan's tokenCeiling:64000 is a no-op) and scrub any plan JSON that sets it. CODE QUALITY: add an ArchitectureTest asserting the one-way dependency (Conductor.Planning must not reference the engine) as PART OF P0. Decide model ownership deliberately (SessionKind is shared vocabulary - move it or a 1:1 twin so the library needs no engine ref). Gate: solution builds with Conductor.Planning standalone; engine depends on it not vice versa (arch test); full existing suite green (behavior unchanged); tokenCeiling grep-clean.

stages.title: Role-to-agent assignment + multi-item sessions
stages.notes: Deliver P1 per docs/history/CONDUCTOR-PLANNER.md (P1). Depends on P0. REUSE: per-stage agent/model/persona overrides, WorkflowStep.Model, PersonaRegistry, the task graph (TaskGraph/TaskWrites/GET tasks), the active-checkpoint selection in SessionRunner. Net-new: IAssignmentPolicy in Conductor.Planning returning a SessionAssignment (resolved agent + the SET of claimed task ids) from rules + ready task graph + session kind; default rule reproduces today (one agent, active checkpoint). Add a role->agent map (deliver/verify/audit/fix -> model+persona) so 'who audits' is DATA not code. Multi-item claim: several ready cards under the active checkpoint, and behind an explicit rule flag conflict-free sibling checkpoints via StageConfig.PathClaims; the prompt lists every claimed item. Engine asks IAssignmentPolicy instead of hard-picking the first checkpoint - loop stays dumb executor, policy stays smart decider. OUT OF SCOPE: full work-queue scheduling (north star, not a run-loop rewrite). Gate: rules assigning audit->a different model spawn the audit session with it; a session claims two conflict-free cards and the prompt names both; a path-conflicting claim is refused by the policy (unit test); single-item plans unchanged.

stages.title: QA policy dial - off / every-session / phase-gate
stages.notes: Deliver P2 per docs/history/CONDUCTOR-PLANNER.md (P2). Depends on P0 (and rides G3 live reload). REUSE: the workflows already ARE these modes (every-session=deliver-verify; phase-gate=big-dev-then-big-audit; off=spike/docs-only or overrides.skipVerification), plus verifierThreshold + WorkflowOverrides + the session-scoped SkipVerificationThisStage flag. Net-new: IQaPolicy in Conductor.Planning - a QaPolicy rule (off|everySession|phaseGate + threshold + audit-covers-all-prior) that RESOLVES to an effective WorkflowDefinition + overrides (no new engine concept, a friendly dial over what exists), settable plan-wide and per-stage. Face: Plan-tab Settings (and per-stage) gains the QA dial + verifierThreshold; edits apply at the next session boundary via G3 reload; demo mirror + golden + key test + contract test. CODE QUALITY: resolving a dial value must produce EXACTLY the same run as selecting the matching workflow by hand today - pin with a unit test comparing resolved definitions. Gate: QA=off runs deliver-only; QA=phaseGate runs deliver x N then one audit+fix over accumulated checkpoints; the dial round-trips through /plan/edit and is honored live after reload.

stages.title: Kanban card detail - prompt building-blocks + edit + AI-assist
stages.notes: Deliver P3 per docs/history/CONDUCTOR-PLANNER.md (P3). Depends on P0. REUSE: PromptBuilder composition, GET /prompt/preview, G1 advisor plumbing (Advisor.AskTextAsync + preview->confirm), the Kanban tab, the task graph, ApplyPlanEdit, /inject. Net-new: (1) a pure PromptComposition - decompose PromptBuilder output into an ordered list of labeled PromptBlock{Kind,Label,Content,Editable} (persona/stage-notes/task/per-task-context/injected-knowledge/tool-contract); pure function of state = previewable + testable; serve at GET /tasks/{id}/prompt. (2) Face card detail: selecting a card opens a panel of the blocks; the TASK-SCOPED blocks are editable (task title + a structured per-task extra-context field) and persist as task data - NOT free-form prompt splicing. (3) AI-assist: 'ask the advisor to refine this item' (reuse G1 advisor, task-scoped, returns a proposed edit you confirm) and 'hand to Claude/another brain' (write an injection/handoff via /inject); both explicit, owner-invoked, token-gated. CODE QUALITY: editing writes STRUCTURED task data, never raw prompt strings; composition stays deterministic; advisor-refine reuses preview->confirm->apply (nothing mutates without confirm). Gate: card detail shows labeled blocks; editing task extra-context changes exactly that block in the recomposed prompt (unit test on the pure composition); advisor-refine applies only on confirm; goldens for the panel.

stages.title: Finish the decoupling - Conductor.Planning stands alone
stages.notes: Deliver P4 per docs/history/CONDUCTOR-PLANNER.md (P4). Depends on P0/P1/P2. REUSE: P0's assembly + interfaces; VerdictEngine.Workflow.cs's 'what next' logic. Net-new: move the remaining workflow/assignment/QA DECISION logic fully behind IWorkflowResolver/IAssignmentPolicy/IQaPolicy; the engine passes POCO facts in and executes decisions out; VerdictEngine keeps EFFECTING verdicts (state/events) but DELEGATES the decision. Standalone-usage proof: a tiny consumer (a test project or tools/plan-lint) that references ONLY Conductor.Planning loads a plan file and prints the resolved workflow + assignment + QA decision for a stage - no engine, no store. CODE QUALITY: no behavior change to real runs (structural move guarded by the suite); the standalone consumer must compile+run with ZERO transitive dependency on Conductor. Gate: the standalone consumer resolves decisions from a plan file using only Conductor.Planning; the architecture test still passes; full engine suite green; no planning-domain type remains in the engine assembly.

stages.title: Session-token rollover + limits surfaced, session-scoped, off by default
stages.notes: Deliver P5 per docs/history/CONDUCTOR-PLANNER.md (P5). Rides G3 live reload; independent of P1-P4. REUSE: limits.maxSessionTokens (null=off by default; when crossed the session ends RolledOver - handoff written, next session fresh, NO attempt burned), limits.softBreakRatio (the 80% wind-down nudge, active only when maxSessionTokens set), and the session-scoped SkipVerificationThisStage/SkipGatesThisStage flag pattern. Net-new: Face surfaces maxSessionTokens + softBreakRatio in the Plan-tab limits as an honestly-labeled 'Session token rollover (DeepSeek-style): OFF' control - editable, with a session-scoped 'this run only' override (new *ThisRun flag in the existing pattern) flipped live via a control verb without touching the plan file; off stays the default. Extend ApplyPlanEdit + the live-limits Settings (from P2) to cover these fields. CODE QUALITY: off-by-default must stay true (absent block changes nothing); the live override is session-scoped state, not a plan-file write, so it evaporates at run end by design. Gate: rollover is visibly OFF by default in the Face; toggling on (plan or this-run) makes a session past the token count end RolledOver with a handoff and no burned attempt; the this-run override never writes the plan file.
